41.018,-75.08563: Shawnee-Minisink Archaeological Site. Nearly 13,000 years old, this location, near the confluence of the Delaware River and Brodhead Creek, is one of the earliest dated Native American sites in the northeastern US. Archaeological investigations uncovered hundreds of stone tools left by the early inhabitants around a series of campfires. Remains of fish and fruit provided evidence of a more diverse diet than expected for the late Ice Age.
41.04,-75.31: Sullivan's March. Learned's Tavern marked the end of the second day's march from Easton to Fort Wyoming, at Wilkes-Barre. The army camped here June 19, 1779, after a 16-mile march from Heller's Tavern.
Sullivan Expedition Against the Iroquois Indians, 1779 (Learned's Tavern)- PLAQUE. The last house on the frontier. The end of the second day's march June 19, 1779. Distance 16 miles.
41.09,-75.01: Fort Hyndshaw. Built in 1756 by order of the Province of Pennsylvania. Northernmost of a line of defenses erected during the French and Indian War.
